newsitem.title: USA: Calif. finds no cause of illness in juice scare.
newsitem.headline: Calif. finds no cause of illness in juice scare.

text.p: California state health officials said they have not identified a specific cause of illnesses in its ongoing investigation related to the consumption of Odwalla Inc's unpasteurized apple juice.

California Department of Health Services' investigators are working with the U.S. Food and Drug Administration and Odwalla Inc to identify the source of contamination, health officials said in a statement late on November 8.
The agency said 54 illnesses have been reported in Washington, Colorado, British Columbia and California in the past two weeks. Earlier reports have attributed the illnesses to E. coli poisoning.
Numerous juice samples are being analyzed and investigators are examining how the product was handled, transported and processed, health officials said.
In the wake of the investigation, health officials are urging consumers to follow standard health practice and always wash all fruits and vegetables before eating them, health officials said.
Odwalla, which is based in Half Moon Bay, Calif., recalled its juice on October 30, 1996, after the an outbreak of E. coli was tied to products containing its apple juice.
Odwalla later reintroduced three juice blends that have been reformulated without apple juice.
